reviewer: Codex primary final critical reading; selected separate-reader findings retained in evidence/reviews. No human/Claude acceptance claimed.

clarity.evidence: One book title and one physical barcode establishes why an edition differs from a borrowable copy.

scope.evidence: Complete circulation answer covers checkout, renewal, return, local-date fines, holds and repair without turning a small library into services.

contracts.evidence: Copy ownership, member slots, loan identity and FIFO assignment tokens agree across methods and trace states.

correctness.evidence: LibraryChecks passes 46 focused checks including copy/member races, calendar dates and stale tokens.

failure_handling.evidence: A returned old loan cannot release a new borrower; expired pickup tokens cannot claim reassigned copies; fine assessment is repeatable without duplicate debt.

tradeoffs.evidence: A single circulation authority versus database transactions, FIFO fairness, renewal policy and overdue calculations are defended.

visual_learning.evidence: LibraryDemo emits three copy/queue histories; stepping shows old-token rejection and current ownership.

code.evidence: examples/learning-java/src/kb/library; full copyable source/download parity and exact excerpts checked by check_review_lot.py; actual runtime output in lot-command-output.json and lot-runtime.json.

rendering.evidence: LLD-9-browser.json: article and walkthrough in light/dark at 1280/390px; theme controls, navigation, no missing images/page-wide overflow, table contrast >=4.5. Per-topic assets resolve.

limits: Local mechanism and fixture checks do not establish remote-provider behavior, distributed durability/failover, production throughput or model quality. Scope-specific boundaries are explicit in the answer.
